newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fall in Japan c/a surplus may have bottomed out-US.
newsitem.headline: Fall in Japan c/a surplus may have bottomed out-US.

text.p: The pace of decline in Japan's current account surplus appears to have bottomed out, Lawrence Greenwood, economic minister-counselor at the U.S. embassy in Tokyo, said on Thursday.

"Starting around the fall of last year the drop in Japan's gobal current account surplus began to bottom out -- appeared to begin to bottom out -- and there are some indications that it might be turning around," he told a news conference.
Greenwood added that some private forecasters had predicted that the current account surplus would increase in 1997.
"Japan needs to maintain sustained domestic demand-led growth and needs to take steps to avoid a resurgence of the current account surplus," he said.
He said Japan and the United States shared the same view on this. "This is a basic area of agreement between the U.S. and Japan in the macro area," he said.
Japan's contentious surplus in its current account, the broadest measure of trade in goods and services, rose sharply in January, marking the first increase in 17 months.
The Finance Ministry said on Thursday that the current account surplus in January totalled 150.7 billion yen against a surplus of 32.6 billion yen a year earlier.
The surplus in merchandise trade alone fell 15.5 percent to 229.3 billion yen.
